title: Pasta e Ceci
subtitle: Roman chickpea and pasta soup with rosemary and chilli
excerpt: Pasta e ceci is a thick Roman soup of chickpeas and short pasta flavoured with rosemary, garlic, and chilli. Half the chickpeas are blended to make the broth creamy, and the pasta cooks directly in the soup and absorbs the flavour as it swells. It is filling, cheap, and takes under 45 minutes.
sourceNotes: Pasta e ceci is a Roman and central Italian classic and one of the oldest documented combinations of pasta and legumes in Italian cooking. It is closely associated with the Roman tradition of 'le minestre di magro', lean soups eaten on fast days (Fridays and during Lent). The Roman version includes anchovies and rosemary; the dish appears in Bartolomeo Scappi's Opera (1570) and has been a staple of Roman home cooking ever since.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze without the pasta. Add fresh pasta when reheating.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the chickpea base ahead. Add pasta just before serving.

content.text: Pasta e ceci is a Roman chickpea soup with short pasta. The base is garlic and rosemary fried in olive oil, chickpeas, and a little tomato, then half blended to thicken the broth. The pasta is cooked directly in the soup and absorbs the chickpea liquid as it swells. Chilli flakes give it a gentle heat. It is one of the cheapest meals in this collection and one of the most satisfying.

items.prepNote: half a tin, or 3 tablespoons of passata

content.text: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the garlic, rosemary, and chilli flakes. Cook for 2 minutes until fragrant and the garlic is golden.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes. Add the chickpeas and stock. Season with salt and bring to a simmer.
Cook for 10 minutes. Use a stick blender to blend about half the soup until smooth. The result should be thick and creamy with some whole chickpeas remaining.
Add the pasta. Cook for the time indicated on the packet, stirring frequently. Add a splash of water if the soup becomes too thick.
Taste and adjust the salt. Serve immediately with a drizzle of raw olive oil in each bowl.

Pasta e ceci is Roman and central Italian, eaten particularly on Fridays as part of the Catholic lean-day tradition. The Roman version is distinctive for its use of rosemary, garlic, and often a couple of anchovy fillets dissolved in the oil at the start of cooking. The anchovy is optional here but adds a lot of depth if you are open to it. The dish is thick and should be almost like a stew rather than a liquid soup.
